summary: Welcome to Vyut Code-a-Thon! Use your Python syllabus knowledge to build a unique, creative, and useful program with your team. Read all the rules and marking criteria carefully before coding in the Interpreter.

sections.heading: 1. Team & Submission Rules
sections.text: Every participant must follow these competition guidelines strictly:
points: **Team Size:** Each team can have a **maximum of 6 students**.
**Single Submission:** All members will plan, write, and test the program together, but **only 1 student (the Team Leader)** will submit the final code.
**One Chance Only:** Only the first submission from each team will be evaluated. Do not submit multiple times.
**Strict No-AI Policy:** Using ChatGPT, Gemini, or the internet to generate code is strictly prohibited. Copy-pasting is disabled in the Interpreter, so you must type your own code.
sections.tip: 💡 **Team Viva Rule:** During evaluation, judges can ask **any random member** of your team to explain how a specific line or loop works. Make sure every team member understands the whole code!

sections.heading: 2. Allowed Syntax, Functions & Operators
sections.text: Your program must be built using the concepts from your curriculum:
points: **Basic Functions & Type Casting:** `print()`, `input()`, `int()`, `float()`, and `#` for comments.
**Loops:** `for` loop, `range()` function, nested `for` loop, and `while` loop.
**Lists:** Creating lists `[]`, indexing/slicing, and methods like `append()`, `insert()`, `extend()`, `remove()`, and `pop()`.
sections.tip: ⚠️ **Special Permission Rule:** If your team wants to use any operator, function, or syntax outside the list above, you **must take prior permission from Gaurav Sir or Manish Sir**. External syntax will only be accepted if explicitly allowed by them.

sections.heading: 3. Point System (Total: 100 Marks)
sections.text: | Category | Marks | Evaluation Criteria |/n| --- | --- | --- |/n| **1. Unique Idea & Usefulness** | **25** | How original and helpful the program is in real life or school (avoid basic book questions like Odd/Even). |/n| **2. Code Accuracy & Syntax** | **25** | The program runs without errors and smartly uses loops, conditions, and lists. |/n| **3. Clean Code & Comments** | **15** | Clear variable names, neat output messages, and proper `#` comments explaining the logic. |/n| **4. Team Viva & Logic Test** | **35** | Any 2 or 3 random members from the team will be asked to explain the code and logic. |

sections.heading: 4. How to Submit Your Project
points: Switch from **Notes** to **Interpreter** using the top slider.
Type your Python program and click **Run** to test it thoroughly with different inputs.
Once your team's final code is ready, click the **Submit** button at the top right.
Enter your **Team Name** and the names of your team members (up to 6 students), then click **Submit Project** before the deadline.

questions.q: Starter Example: Mini School Canteen Billing System
questions.answer: Here is a small example showing how you can combine `while` loop, `if-elif-else`, `and`/`or` operators, `int()`, and `lists` to make a useful project. **Do not copy this—create your own unique idea!**
questions.code:
# Mini Canteen Billing Demo
items = []
total = 0
run = 1

print("--- Welcome to School Canteen ---")

while run == 1:
    print("1. Samosa (Rs 10)  2. Sandwich (Rs 25)  3. Exit & Bill")
    choice = int(input("Enter your choice (1/2/3): "))

    if choice == 1:
        items.append("Samosa")
        total = total + 10
        print("Samosa added!")
    elif choice == 2:
        items.append("Sandwich")
        total = total + 25
        print("Sandwich added!")
    elif choice == 3:
        run = 0
    else:
        print("Invalid choice! Please select 1, 2 or 3.")

print("--- Final Bill ---")
print("Items ordered:", items)
print("Total Amount: Rs", total)
algorithm: Create an empty list 'items' and set 'total' to 0 and 'run' to 1
Run a while loop as long as 'run' is equal to 1
Show the menu and take the user's choice using int(input())
Use if-elif-else to add the chosen item to the list and add its price to 'total'
If user enters 3, set 'run' to 0 to stop the loop
Print the final list of items and the total bill amount
